blockers.message: the review record has no `## plan.challenge` section, while roles were active at it
R-privacy-1 (Looked-up e-mail address written to the error log) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it
R-privacy-2 (Chat vendor receives phone, birth date and address it does not need) is high and still open; fix it, or a human accepts the risk or defers it

findings.evidence: throw new NotFoundError(`no customer with e-mail ${email}`);
findings.recommendation: Keep the e-mail address out of the error message (for example `throw new NotFoundError("no customer for this e-mail")`). As it stands, every lookup that matches no customer reaches `errorHandler` in src/server.ts, which runs `logger.error("request failed", { path: req.path, error: err.message })`, so the address an agent typed — a customer's or a mistyped one — lands in the application logs with no retention rule (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c) data minimisation, Art. 32).
findings.title: Looked-up e-mail address written to the error log

findings.evidence:
id: String(customer.id),
name: customer.name,
email: customer.email,
phone: customer.phone,
birthDate: customer.birth_date,
address: customer.address,
findings.recommendation: Send Helply only what the stated purpose needs — greeting the signed-in customer by name so the agent knows who they talk to: the opaque id and the name (the e-mail only if the agent console needs it to match the account). Drop `phone`, `birthDate` and `address`; also stop selecting them in `customerById` (src/support.ts:28) since nothing else uses them. Today `GET /chat/settings` hands the full record to the browser and the widget forwards it to the third-party processor (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c), Art. 25, Art. 28).
findings.title: Chat vendor receives phone, birth date and address it does not need

findings.evidence: "SELECT id, email, name, phone, birth_date, address FROM customers WHERE lower(email) = lower($1)",
findings.recommendation: The proposal's purpose is that agents stop asking customers who they are; confirm with the team which fields an agent needs to identify the customer and return only those from `POST /support/customers/lookup` (src/routes.ts:7). Birth date, phone and postal address go to every support agent on each lookup without a stated need (GDPR Art. 5(1)(c)). Low confidence: the agents' actual need is not stated in the plan.
findings.title: Support lookup returns the whole customer record

findings.recommendation: A question for the team, not a code fix: state in the plan whether Helply is covered by a processor agreement (GDPR Art. 28), where it stores data (Chapter V if outside the EEA), how long it keeps chat users' data, and how a customer's erasure or access request reaches the copy Helply holds (Art. 15–17). Only the controller can say what was decided.
findings.title: Helply as processor: transfer, retention and erasure not identified

findings.recommendation: Use a message without the identifier ("no customer for this session"); `errorHandler` logs `err.message`, so the signed-in customer's id ends up in the logs. The impact is limited to a session whose customer no longer exists.
findings.title: Customer id written to the error log
